The core insight is that in uncertain environments, naive Kelly betting on perceived probabilities leads to suboptimal outcomes due to estimation errors. The expected log-growth formula E[g] = 2(δ² - σ²)Φ(δ/σ) + 2σδφ(δ/σ) quantifies this trade-off. When estimation error dominates (σ > δ), the expected growth becomes negative, even if the true edge is positive. This motivates a gate condition: only bet when |δ_perc| > σ, which ensures that the perceived edge exceeds the estimation error magnitude. The derivation assumes even odds and small δ, but can be extended to general odds using similar stochastic control principles. The failure mode occurs when estimation error is underestimated or when the assumption of normality breaks down. Dualities emerge in that the same framework applies to both risk management and strategic decision-making under uncertainty.
